## 1. Purpose

This SOP describes the field operation of the Hach DR900 portable
colorimeter for on-site water quality analysis. The DR900 enables
rapid, field-based measurement of nutrients, metals, and other
parameters using Hach pre-packaged reagent kits. Field colorimetry
provides same-day results when samples cannot be transported to the
lab within required hold times, and it supports real-time decisions
during stormwater events, spill response, or reconnaissance sampling.

This SOP focuses on field-specific procedures (transport, outdoor
operation, field QC). For detailed method chemistry, reagent handling,
the Method Registry, and laboratory use of the DR3900 and DR900, see
[SOP-L303 Hach Colorimetric Analysis](../lab_sops/SOP-L303-hach-colorimetric.qmd).


## 2. Scope

- **Applies to:** Field use of the Hach DR900 portable colorimeter at
  EA Program field sites for grab-sample analysis of nutrients (PO~4~,
  NO~3~, NH~3~), metals (Fe, Mn, Cu), and general chemistry
  (hardness, chloride, silica, chlorine)
- **Does not apply to:** Laboratory bench-top analysis (see
  [SOP-L303](../lab_sops/SOP-L303-hach-colorimetric.qmd)); field
  turbidity (see [SOP-F205](SOP-F205-handheld-turbidity-meter.qmd));
  in situ sonde-based measurements (see
  [SOP-F200](SOP-F200-eureka-manta2.qmd))
- **Location:** All EA Program surface water, groundwater, and
  stormwater field sites


## 3. Responsibilities

| Role              | Responsibility                                          |
|:------------------|:--------------------------------------------------------|
| PI / Field Lead   | Select analytes and approve field methods               |
| Trained Personnel | Operate the DR900 per this SOP; record results          |
| New Students      | Complete training on both this SOP and SOP-L303 before
                      independent field use                                |


## 4. Safety and Hazards

::: {.callout-warning}
### Hazards

- **Chemical:** Hach reagent powder pillows and liquid reagents may
  contain acids, oxidizers, or heavy metal indicators. Review the SDS
  for each kit before field use. Some reagents (e.g., cadmium in older
  nitrate methods) are classified as hazardous waste.
- **Physical:** Glass sample vials can break during field transport.
  Pack in padded cases.
- **Biological:** Water samples may contain pathogens. Wear gloves.
:::

### Required PPE

- [ ] Nitrile gloves
- [ ] Safety glasses (required for all reagent handling)
- [ ] Closed-toed shoes or wading boots

### Emergency Procedures

For reagent splashes to skin or eyes, flush with clean water for at
least 15 minutes. Carry a squeeze bottle of DI water for emergency
rinsing. Refer to
[SOP-F001 Field Safety](SOP-F001-field-safety.qmd) and
[SOP-L003 Hazardous Materials Handling](../lab_sops/SOP-L003-hazardous-materials-handling.qmd).


## 5. Equipment and Materials

| Item                                  | Notes                                    |
|:--------------------------------------|:-----------------------------------------|
| Hach DR900 Portable Colorimeter       | Confirm battery level; charge before field day |
| Sample vials (10 mL, 25 mL, 1-inch round) | Matched to the methods being run     |
| Hach reagent kits (powder pillows or TNT vials) | Select analytes per project needs; check expiration dates |
| DI water (squeeze bottle, 500 mL minimum) | For blanks, rinsing, and dilutions   |
| Lint-free wipes (Kimwipes)            | For cleaning vial exteriors              |
| Silicone oil and applicator cloth     | For 1-inch round vials                   |
| Timer                                 | Phone timer or stopwatch for reaction times |
| Graduated cylinder or pipette         | For measured sample volumes              |
| Waste container (sealable)            | For used reagent vials and waste solution |
| Padded carrying case                  | For protecting vials during transport    |
| Field notebook                        | For recording results and QC data        |
| Ziplock bags                          | For isolating used reagent packets       |


## 6. Procedure

### 6.1 Pre-Field Preparation

1. Identify the analytes to be measured in the field and pack the
   corresponding reagent kits. Verify that none are expired.
2. Pack sufficient DI water for blanks and rinsing (a minimum of
   500 mL for a typical sampling event).
3. Pack at least two extra clean sample vials per method.
4. Charge the DR900 battery. Confirm the stored programs for your
   methods are accessible on the instrument.
5. Print or photograph the method procedure cards for each analyte
   (from the kit box or
   [SOP-L303](../lab_sops/SOP-L303-hach-colorimetric.qmd) Method
   Registry).

### 6.2 Field Setup

1. Set up the DR900 on a flat, stable surface out of direct sunlight.
   Direct sunlight on the sample chamber produces erroneous readings.
2. If no shade is available, use a jacket, tarp, or your body to
   shade the instrument during reading.
3. Turn on the DR900 and allow it to complete its self-check.
4. Select the stored program for your analyte (see
   [SOP-L303](../lab_sops/SOP-L303-hach-colorimetric.qmd), Section 6).

### 6.3 Blank and Calibration Check

1. Fill a clean sample vial with DI water to the line.
2. Wipe the vial exterior with a lint-free cloth.
3. Insert the vial, close the lid, and press **Zero**.
4. The display should read 0.00 (within the method detection limit).
   If it does not, clean the vial and re-zero.
5. If a known standard is available (mid-range Hach standard), run it
   after zeroing. The result should be within +/- 10% of the stated
   value. Record the result in the field notebook.

### 6.4 Sample Analysis

Follow the method-specific procedure from the reagent kit or
[SOP-L303](../lab_sops/SOP-L303-hach-colorimetric.qmd) Method Registry.
The general workflow is:

1. Collect a grab sample per
   [SOP-F300](SOP-F300-surface-water-sampling.qmd).
2. Fill the sample vial to the line with the sample.
3. Add the reagent (powder pillow, liquid dropper, or TNT vial) per
   the method instructions.
4. Cap, invert, and mix as directed. Start the timer for the required
   reaction time.
5. When the reaction time is complete, wipe the vial exterior with a
   lint-free cloth (apply silicone oil for round vials).
6. Insert the vial into the DR900, close the lid (shading from
   sunlight), and press **Read**.
7. Record the result in the field notebook: analyte, method number,
   sample ID, reading, units, date, and time.
8. Rinse the vial 3 times with DI water before the next sample.

### 6.5 Waste Management

1. Collect all used reagent packets, vials, and waste solution in a
   sealable container or ziplock bag.
2. Do not discard reagent waste in the field.
3. Return waste to the lab and dispose of per
   [SOP-L003](../lab_sops/SOP-L003-hazardous-materials-handling.qmd).
   Cadmium-containing reagents (NitraVer 5 older formulation) are
   hazardous waste.


## 7. Quality Control

- Zero the instrument with DI water before each batch of samples.
- Run one DI blank and one mid-range standard at the start of each
  field session. Record results in the field notebook.
- Analyze one field duplicate per 10 samples (minimum one per event).
  Duplicate RPD should be < 20% for concentrations above 5 times the
  detection limit.
- If the field blank reads above the method detection limit,
  investigate contamination (dirty vials, contaminated DI water) and
  re-run.
- Note ambient temperature in the field notebook. Some Hach methods
  are temperature-sensitive; if the sample temperature is outside the
  method-specified range (typically 20--25 C), allow the sample to
  equilibrate or note the potential bias.

## 10. Training Record

Before using the DR900 in the field independently, personnel must:

1. Read this SOP and
   [SOP-L303 Hach Colorimetric Analysis](../lab_sops/SOP-L303-hach-colorimetric.qmd)
   in full
2. Demonstrate a complete field analysis (zero, standard check, sample
   analysis, waste collection) under supervision
3. Be signed off by the PI or field lead
